sections.h2: Which office sets value and which sends the bill
sections.html:
The sheriff sends bills and takes the money. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA), at (502) 348-1810, sets value. The sheriff never assesses anything, so complaints about a figure belong at the PVA.

What lands in your mailbox depends on the district. The sheriff collects for the state, the county and school districts, and where a contract exists for cities and special districts as well.

  • Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13: county bill alone.
  • District 2: county plus the City of New Haven.
  • District 3: county schools plus the City of Bardstown.
  • District 4: county, Bardstown city and Bardstown Independent Schools.
  • District 5: county plus Bardstown Independent Schools.
  • District 9: county plus the City of Fairfield.

A house inside Bardstown can generate several bills, so gather all of them before asking for a payoff.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Nelson County
sections.html:
Nelson County became the fourth Kentucky county in 1784, carved from Jefferson County, and spans about 418 square miles of land. Bardstown, the seat, ranks among the state's oldest cities and counted 13,567 people in 2020. The area calls itself the Bourbon Capital of the World, and Heaven Hill, Barton 1792, Willett and Lux Row operate in and near town.

The sheriff's patrol area runs through Bardstown, Bloomfield, New Haven, Fairfield, Boston, Chaplin and New Hope, so one county holds several distinct town markets. Bardstown grows around the crossing of U.S. 31E, U.S. 62 and U.S. 150, with the Bluegrass Parkway just to the south, and the county is part of the Louisville combined statistical area. Bardstown City Schools and Nelson County Schools both operate here, and Nelson County High School stands within the boundaries of the Bardstown district, so buyers should check which district an address falls in.

The population estimate for July 2025 is 49,036, up 4.9% from the 2020 base. There are 21,097 housing units, and 222 building permits were issued in 2025, so resale listings compete with newly built homes.

Owners occupy 78.3% of homes. The midpoint for an owned house is $238,000. Monthly costs run $1,379 with a mortgage and $473 with none, and gross rent has a midpoint of $1,008. Household income has a midpoint of $69,562. About 90.3% of residents had not moved in the past year. The average commute is 26.6 minutes, and employment grew 3.8% from 2022 to 2023.

The bourbon industry shows in the local economy, and Bardstown adds history to the draw. Its Old Talbott Tavern dates to 1779, and the town has a federally listed historic district and a Civil War museum. My Old Kentucky Home State Park hosts The Stephen Foster Story each summer, and the Basilica of St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral recalls the 1808 founding of the Diocese of Bardstown. The Kentucky Bourbon Festival draws visitors to town each year.

Tourism helps resale demand near the old town, but each house still sells on its own condition, tax status and school district.

KRS 134.015 gives the pattern.

What each payment date costs in Nelson County
If paidEffect on the bill
Up to November 1Two percent knocked off
Between November 2 and December 31Bill stands as printed
During JanuaryFive percent extra
February 1 through April 15Twenty-one percent extra

Anything unpaid at the sheriff by April 15 passes to the County Clerk.

The sheriff returns any check that differs from the bill by even a dollar, as well as late or partial ones, because audit rules demand exact accounting. If a lender escrows your tax, send the bill to the lender. The first proper payment received gets processed, and no refund goes to an owner who pays ahead of the lender.

Begin at the PVA, which holds a conference with the owner or a representative. KRS 133.120 requires it before any formal appeal, and a phone call can count. The tax roll is displayed for 13 days beginning the opening Monday in May under KRS 133.045, and the conference must fall before or during that stretch.

A disagreement that survives the conference becomes a written petition at the County Clerk. It lists the parcel, the reasons and the owner's estimate, and it is due the workday after inspection closes. Hearings are public, and the owner supplies the facts: sales listings, insurance policies, construction costs or loan papers. The bill itself isn't delayed, and an increase is billed with interest from the original due date.

Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled, are eligible. The state figure of $49,100 applies to 2025 and 2026 and comes off assessed value before rates. The Nelson County PVA takes the filing, and a passport, birth certificate or license shows age. Disability claims renew each year, except for owners with a service-connected disability and for owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by federal Social Security or the state retirement system.

The tax is a personal debt of the January 1 owner, and delinquent property carries a lien for eleven years under KRS 134.420. A buyer's title company searches for it.

  • Collect every bill for the parcel, including city and independent school lines for a Bardstown address.
  • Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff on the planned closing date.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address for tax bills into the deed, per KRS 382.135.
  • For an inherited house, the executor files an affidavit with the County Clerk naming recipients and values.

A New Haven or Bardstown city bill is separate from the county bill, so a payoff quoting only the county number leaves a gap. Confirm the payoff in writing and keep the receipt with the closing file.

sections.h2: If the house needs work or taxes are behind
sections.html:
Selling with taxes owed is common. The closing agent pays the payoff from your proceeds, so the number you need is the full amount across every bill, not just the county line. After April 15 the clerk quotes it instead of the sheriff. A cash buyer who accepts the house as-is lets you skip repairs and showings, and you can set the closing around the payoff date.

For an heir, the executor's affidavit comes first, then the deed. Bring your photo ID, the latest bills for every district line on the parcel, and any exemption approval. After closing, tell the PVA about the new owner so the next set of bills goes to the right address.

If the house sits in a city district, check which bills the buyer will inherit. A Bardstown address may carry city and independent school lines that a county-only quote misses, and a New Haven or Fairfield address has its own city line. Ask the sheriff which districts apply to your parcel number before you sign a contract, so the payoff you quote the buyer is complete.

faqs.q: Which office handles a Nelson County valuation complaint?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (502) 348-1810. The sheriff doesn't assess property.

faqs.q: Does the Nelson County Sheriff take inexact payments?
faqs.a: No. A check that doesn't match the bill exactly, along with any late or partial payment, is returned.

faqs.q: What becomes of a Nelson County bill still open after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves from the sheriff to the Nelson County Clerk.

faqs.q: Do bills differ across Nelson County?
faqs.a: Yes. Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13 get one county bill, while districts 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9 also receive New Haven, Bardstown, Bardstown Independent School or Fairfield bills.

faqs.q: What deduction does a senior get on a Nelson County home?
faqs.a: The state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026, after an owner who is 65 or over, or totally disabled, applies at the PVA.
